title: Another campy new musical gone too soon… let’s talk about Once Upon A...
transcript: Welcome back to another Broadway post mortem. Today we're going to be talking about once upon a one more time, which is a show that, against my better judgment, I actually really liked. I've talked about this before on this app, but I was at the second preview of once upon a one more time, and I really did not care for it in the state that it was in. And I think a lot of people felt the same way. The early word of mouth for the show was not very positive, and it really wasn't until a couple weeks in that friends started going and telling me, hey, you should give it another shot. It's gotten a lot better. And it wasn't until I went back once the show was frozen that I actually really enjoyed it that second time around and even went back for a third time for their closing performance. And I do have to wonder if that early negative word of mouth is really what killed any momentum that the show could have had. And had they opened with the version that they ended up with, if things would have been a little bit different for them, and that's not to say that there still wouldn't have been challenges for them, I don't think critics were ever really going to like this show. And I think that it is in many ways a victim of poor timing, coming off the heels of several very Similar shows that includes jukebox musicals like Anne Juliette and Moulin Rouge, both of which feature Britney Spears songs in them, as well as musicals like six and even the recent into the Woods revival, which are very similar thematically. I also think that in general, Broadway audiences are becoming more and more cynical when it comes to these big IP musicals, if that's what you wanna call them. And they're often judging them just as cash grabs based on concept alone and not really giving them a chance. I think all of these factors, in combination with the negative word of mouth that the show had at the beginning of its run, really LED to the show not being able to find its audience. Which is a shame, because like I said, I actually think it's a really fun musical. And I think that Broadway needs more fun camping musicals. I'm not gonna claim that the show was perfect by any stretch of the imagination, but I think what it did well, it did really well, and that was it. Nailed the fun and nailed the humor and nailed the tone. The choreography is amazing. The music, obviously, is really great. And of course, the cast, which was absolutely stacked. Obviously, you have Jensen Mard and Justin Greenie stealing every single scene that they are in. But you also have up and comers like Ayesha Jackson in her first Broadway principal role. You have Morgan Whitley as Princess in The pea giving this insane comedic perform. But truly, the entire cast was fantastic and just giving it there all every single night. And so, while this show wasn't necessarily able to find an audience on Broadway, I do have some hope for the future of this show. Hopefully, it goes out on tour. I think it will be really popular at regional theaters. And ultimately, I'm just really excited for more people across America to realize what a fun show this is.
showTitle: Once Upon a One More Time
